## Final result and precise application

**Constructed and kernel checked; independent review pending.** No production authority.
The frozen module is `YulangClosure.BoundedAncestryR61`, SHA-256 `9e1c783016bc14487dd0a4ebc2839dfab0dc3daf911ee88fa02f3624e2ad60a4`.
All 50 authored theorem bodies are retained verbatim in the final audited stdin,
with their exact existing transitive definitions and 46 used inherited theorem bodies.

`initial_success_refines_directed_retained_ancestry` quantifies arbitrary base
Native, all seven source dependency parent projections, an independent visitor
budget, both query IDs, the invocation's allocation outcomes, initial State and
final Resource. Its explicit premises are successful `start` and a finite
successful source-order `Run`; its conclusion is parent-to-descendant R47
`RelationPath` plus an actual R47 `ancestryCheck` list witness. `enqueue_preserves`,
`scan_preserves`, `step_sound` and `successful_run_ancestry` prove it from the
pending-node path invariant, without assuming ancestry or reader soundness.
Both Replay parents are projected in stored lower/upper order. LIFO is cons/pop;
seen is updated on pop, so queued duplicate parents remain duplicated. Source
metadata unused by the visitor is not interpreted; original Rust records retain it.

`native` constructs existing R57 relation records by raw vector position, with
one supplied owner tag, preserving their original endpoint payloads and every
physical/source inventory. It constructs dependencies from the entire ordered
record vector, flattening both Replay parents. This is a model constructor, not
proof that Rust pointer owners have those Nat interpretations. For an existing
Native, `native_eq_existing_of_owner_coordinates` and
`call_success_on_the_existing_owner` use explicit raw index/state and dependency
projection equations to retain exactly that same Native. These equations are
inventory coordinates, not target ancestry assumptions; the source extraction
that establishes them remains OPEN.

`call_success_constructs_witness`, `callback_success_has_ancestry` and
`constructed_ancestry_read_is_sound` construct the successful ancestry policy.
The callback computes the visitor for a selected per-query reservation schedule;
it accepts only observed success. Meta fuel is an observation bound: `None`
means incomplete observation and is unavailable. It is not a native failure or a
proof of native unavailability. Callback API erasure maps such incompleteness to
unavailable SearchLimit, so no exact failure/availability equivalence is claimed.
The successful-Run theorem itself has no meta-fuel hypothesis.

`later_entry_policy_has_directed_ancestry` applies this result to the exact later
Entry policy call, giving use-root -> physical-relation ancestry.
`first_entry_policy_exposes_receipt_ancestry` gives the checked Internal receipt's
use-root -> receipt-relation ancestry. It deliberately does not equate the
externally supplied Internal receipt relation with the physical relation;
actual Internal-root/source extraction remains OPEN. Catch bypasses the visitor.
`successful_candidates_with_constructed_ancestry` instantiates the existing R60
LocalDecode/R59 complete candidate/R49 consumer theorem on the very same Native
and Inputs. The Internal primitive, actual successful outer Run, Checked goal
and terminal equality remain explicit. It does not assume candidate completeness
or concrete LocalDecode; R60 supplies the latter by construction.

## Falsifiers and source ordering

Checked witnesses cover both Replay-parent omissions; reversed edges; initial
query-index-before-inventory/allocation error; oversized reflexive rejection;
pending-before-seen reservation order; same identical query with different
reservation outcomes; invalid parent before visited suppression; unreachable
malformed parent versus reached failure; cyclic exhaustion; duplicate unseen
parent pushes; duplicate-record allocation failure; reordered-record LIFO/work
outcomes; pop work before reflexive acceptance; overflow before work limit;
charging nonmatching dependency records; seen-pop charging without rescanning;
and a fresh zero counter for every call. Reorder witnesses include both a small
explicit budget and the actual 65,536 budget after an explicit bounded prefix.
They do not imply arbitrary prefix reachability from `start`.
No failure, exhaustion, or incomplete observation produces ancestry evidence.

## First remaining source premise and parent status

The frozen Rust `SuccessfulAncestryCall` carries the query, exact State pointer
and complete indexed relation/dependency slices only after one actual successful
`require_relation_ancestry`. It stores no visited path or reservation/work trace.
The first unproved source step is interpreting that same pointer-anchored owner
and seven-constructor parent projection as this exact Native/record inventory,
and deriving a successful model `start`/`Run` (or successful `call` with adequate
observation fuel and the corresponding invocation choices) from that native
success. No theorem assumes a `FaithfulExtraction` or the ancestry conclusion
as a premise. This packet supplies the constructive success-refinement lemma;
it does not establish Rust-to-Run correspondence.

General arbitrary allocation-failure trace equivalence remains explicitly OPEN:
identical queries may allocate differently on separate calls; the concrete
same-query witness rejects replacing these histories with one purported pure
native success function. Actual pointer/Nat interpretation, Internal-root
extraction, outer Rust-to-Run/resource simulation, complete Context/R50/source
interpretation, publication, original A/B, InferenceSoundness, principality,
termination, complete hygiene, executor/runtime safety and production remain
OPEN. All original quantifiers, accepted features and shared witnesses remain.

and no noncomputable wrapper is used in the final source or audit. Proof/slicing
failures and warning-bearing passes remain in their original receipts.

The primary authorized bounded source slices within unchanged -M1024/120s limits.
Only unused **inherited theorem declarations** are omitted; all definitions,
instances, inductives, structures and authored R61 declarations remain original.
The archived slice manifest records module, theorem name, original byte offsets,
original declaration SHA and retained/omitted flag for all 245 inherited roots.
The retained closure is computed by identifier occurrence over the unchanged
remaining source, including bodies of retained lemmas, until fixed point; doc and
omit prefixes travel with their declaration. Missing dependencies are rejected
by Lean; no axiom/opaque stub, assumption, changed body, or checker bypass is used.
The final receipt prints all 96 retained roots' complete types and transitive
axiom sets. The other 199 inherited theorems are not claimed freshly rechecked
here; their previous full-cone receipts stay in frozen R60. All 50 authored roots
are newly checked and printed, without exception.

For the exact final stdin reconstruction, remove only local `import YulangClosure…`
lines, delete only the manifest's omitted byte ranges, concatenate in the archived
source_hashes order, then append the archived #check/#print commands. The only
extra elaboration options after the original Std import are `Elab.async false`
and `compiler.extract_closed false`. The latter is the pinned compiler's closed
term cache switch (Lean/Compiler/LCNF/ConfigOptions.lean), not a proof-checking
switch. Normal kernel checking remains enabled. Every declaration byte and the
complete final stdin reconstruction were authenticated against the receipt.
No environment, cache, worktree, scratch, target or other output path was created.
